Independent mpmath incomplete-gamma normalization checks at p=1001
correctness.rationale: Set ε=1/(p−1). The radial p-harmonic equation gives Cap_p(B_R)^ε=1/I_ε with I_ε=∫_R^∞S(t)^(-ε)dt. Replacing S by C t^k e^(h t) gives C^(-ε)(hε)^(kε−1)Γ(1−kε,hεR). For t>=R the log of the multiplicative relative error O(1/t) affects hε I_ε by O(ε² log(1/ε)), genuinely smaller than the requested ε term. Γ(1−kε,hεR)=1+ε(kγ_E−hR)+o(ε), and the explicit factors give the displayed coefficient with correct h^(m−1−k) scaling. Checked both k=0 and k>0 and the fixed-radius lower-end effect. Independently numerically evaluated exact incomplete-gamma model integrals at p=1001 for multiple C,h,k,R,m examples; the limiting formula is established symbolically, not by numerical fitting.
residual_risks: The area asymptotic is assumed, not proved for all geometries.
The coefficient is pointwise for fixed R; no uniformity for R=R(p) or nonradial comparison.

evidence: Jin–Yin Theorem 1.9 provides a high-p rank-sensitive log term with O(1/p) but not an explicit C-dependent limit.

value.rationale: The formerly unresolved O(1/p) term in a geometric capacity asymptotic becomes an explicit scale-invariant coefficient when first-order sphere growth is known, recovering the volume amplitude C and fixed radius R instead of merely geometric rank. This is a naturally motivated endpoint refinement of an existing open quantitative remainder, not an arbitrary parameter substitution; it gives a directly usable formula for a nontrivial infinite class of model manifolds. Its technical depth is limited to a careful radial Laplace/incomplete-gamma expansion, and no general nonradial theorem is claimed.
residual_risks: If a standard published general regular-variation theorem explicitly yields this normalized next coefficient, the value/priority may diminish; stronger relative asymptotic is a real hypothesis.

final_claim: For complete rotationally symmetric model manifolds with S(r)=C r^k e^{h r}(1+O(r^−1)) (C,h>0,k>=0), fixed R>0 and dimension m, the normalized radial p-capacity Q_p equals 1+[k log(p-1)+log(C h^(m−1−k))+hR−k EulerGamma]/(p-1)+o(1/p).
limitations: Requires fixed R and a relative O(r^-1) area expansion with h>0 and C>0; no family-wide validity of that hypothesis.
No nonradial capacities, moving radii or sharp uniform error rate claimed.
The calculation is an elementary incomplete-gamma asymptotic once the strong relative sphere-area hypothesis is made; a generic Laplace/Wilson-Watson expansion could subsume it.
The hyperbolic k=0 instance may already be implicit in exact formulas and is explicitly not a new theorem by itself.
